title: Reserve rotation and surge policy schedule for dedicated capacity
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: create an operational schedule and policy for rotating reserved pools, predictable surge lanes, and fallback surge policies to reduce wasted reservation cost while guaranteeing latency SLAs for paid Dedicated customers. Background: customers have asked for better predictability on reserved GPU utilization and clearer behavior during bursts. We need a plan that ties forecasting cadence, reservoir rotation windows, canary and rollback steps, and cost guardrails into a repeatable quarterly playbook. Scope: define rotation cadence (daily/weekly/monthly windows), surge reservation staging (prewarm vs on-demand), policy precedence (priority buckets, fairshare), observable signals for trigger and rollback, billing implications, and runbook steps for SRE and Account teams. Out of scope: changes to pricing model and long-term hedging algorithm (separate initiative).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A written schedule and formal policy doc published in Confluence with clear rotation windows and surge lane definitions; 2) Implementation checklist created and reviewed by Eng and SRE; 3) Canary plan validated in staging with two dedicated customers in Feb cycle and rollback mechanics tested; 4) Dashboards (utilization, prewarm hit rate, excess-reservation-hours) instrumented and linked; 5) Cost delta projection (expected savings vs. risk) presented to GTM; 6) Operational runbook with owner assignments and on-call playbook included
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: over-aggressive rotation causes cold starts and latency SLO violations; Mitigation: conservative prewarm buffer + progressive canary;
Risk: mismatched billing expectations for customers on committed plans; Mitigation: GTM communication templates and opt-out windows;
Risk: autoscale policy complexity increases operational toil; Mitigation: provide a simplified default policy and an advanced policy for power users;
